title: Stabilization of a closed inverse system with finitely presented limit
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a nonempty directed set, and $(U_i,q_i,r_{ji})$ an inverse system of $S$-schemes, where $q_i:U_i\to S$ and $r_{ji}:U_j\to U_i$ for $j\ge i$ satisfy $q_i\circ r_{ji}=q_j$. Assume each $U_i$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], each $q_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and each transition $r_{ji}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $(U,(\rho_i))$ be its inverse limit in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], with induced morphism $q:U\to S$. If $q$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then there exists $i_0\in I$ such that every projection $\rho_i:U\to U_i$ for $i\ge i_0$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 081B, label lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed, clause (3), applied to the identity of the limit

proof.text: Fix a stage a and choose a finite affine open cover U_t of D_a, using quasi-compactness. For each U_t restrict the diagram to Over(a) and take the restricted limiting cone using isLimitOpensCone. Affine transitions make each restricted stage affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The restricted structure maps remain locally of finite type; the limit structure map remains locally of finite presentation after composition with the open immersion into the original limit.

For each restricted system E with limit V and structure map q_V, apply Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation to the identity of V. Obtain a stage i and a morphism g:E_i to V with rho_i followed by g equal to the identity and g followed by q_V equal to the stage structure map.

The maps g followed by rho_i and the identity of E_i are maps over S to the locally finite type target E_i. Their pullbacks to V agree. Apply Scheme.exists_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType to obtain h:k to i with E(h) followed by g followed by rho_i equal to E(h). For every j mapping to k, let h_ji:j to i be the composite and put v=E(h_ji) followed by g. The cone equation gives rho_j followed by v equal to the identity. Postcompose v followed by rho_j with E(h_ji); the descended equality gives E(h_ji). Transitions are monomorphisms (closed immersions before open restriction, monomorphic also after restriction), so cancellation gives v followed by rho_j equal to the identity. Thus every such rho_j is an isomorphism.

Take an upper bound b of a and the finitely many underlying stage indices k_t in the directed set; Finset.exists_le also applies to an empty family. For i at least b, the inverse images of the U_t cover D_i and each restriction of rho_i to these opens is the isomorphism just constructed (transporting the domain along the cone preimage identity). Isomorphisms are local on the target by the gluing of their unique local inverses, so rho_i is an isomorphism. Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_iSup_eq_top implements this gluing. The empty cover is included.
